# Mirage mod API reference

Every function a mod can call, in `MirageApi`'s order (ABI v1 only grows: entries are appended, never changed), with what `loader/include/mirage/api.h` says about it. The same API is `mirage.*` in Lua, the `mirage::` wrappers in C++ (`mirage/mirage.hpp`) and `Mod`, `Module` and `GameObject` in C#. Calls marked "game thread" run from a module's tick, an event or a hook; a newer function is checked with `MIRAGE_API_HAS(api, field)` when a mod may run on an older runtime.

## Function hooks

Game thread. Hooks of one function run by priority, higher first. A native function (FUNC_Native) can be hooked before and after, without parameters; one called by native index from script isn't seen at all. NULL when it can't be hooked (the log says why); a function not loaded yet (a level's) is hooked when it is. Removed at the mod's unload.

### `hook_function`

```c
MirageHook*(MIRAGE_CALL* hook_function)(MirageMod* mod, const char* function, int32_t when, int32_t priority, MirageHookFn fn, void* user);
```

### `hook_remove`

```c
void(MIRAGE_CALL* hook_remove)(MirageHook* hook);
```

## More game objects

Game thread. ---------------------------------------------------------------- The live objects of a class or its subclasses: `class_name` is a short name ("GameEngine") or a path ("Engine.GameEngine"). Class default objects ("Default__GameEngine") only with MIRAGE_OBJECTS_DEFAULTS. Copies up to `capacity` handles into `out` (may be NULL) and returns how many there are; -1 when no such class is loaded. Like any MirageObject, look them up again rather than keep them across ticks.

### `objects_of_class`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* objects_of_class)(const char* class_name, uint32_t flags, MirageObject** out, int32_t capacity);
```

## The player and input

Only for a change seen in that physics step (the engine starts it over when the move changes within a tick); a change seen at the end of a tick is reported after the game handled it, and skipping it does nothing. Anywhere else: nothing.

## The game's input

The player's own while they play (not while the menu is open: the game doesn't get it then), a TAS macro's while one records or plays. Key names are the engine's, any case: "W", "SpaceBar", "LeftMouseButton", "MouseScrollUp", "one". Any thread. Without the monitor (a build without the TAS engine) input_key_state returns 0: read the keyboard yourself.

## The generated SDK

The SDK's headers are public: a native mod that links mirage::sdk sets its globals from these once (in mirage_mod_load), then reads game objects directly: void* names; void* objects; api->sdk_globals(&names, &objects); Classes::FName::GNames = (decltype(Classes::FName::GNames))names; ... GObjects likewise Memory the SDK reaches is the game's: the game thread only, like every game object.

### `sdk_globals`

```c
void(MIRAGE_CALL* sdk_globals)(void** gnames, void** gobjects);
```

## The player's state

Game thread. player_state_capture copies up to `capacity` bytes and returns the full length (0: no player, or the layout of the game's values couldn't be worked out). player_state_apply puts one back: 1 done, 0 not (another level, another player class, no player, the player can't be moved now; the log says which). Every apply counts in mirage.shared("mirage", "save_state.loads").

### `player_state_capture`

```c
uint32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* player_state_capture)(char* buffer, uint32_t capacity);
```


```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* module_set_state)(const char* name, int32_t on);
```

Back to plain walking: out of a death fall, a slide, stuck input Any module, by name (another mod's too), switched on or off as the player would. 0: no such module. Any thread.

## The menu's ImGui for a native mod built against the same ImGui

The mod calls ImGui::SetCurrentContext(ctx) and ImGui::SetAllocatorFunctions(alloc, free, user) in each of its render callbacks (loader/include/mirage/imgui.hpp does it). MirageUi is the stable way: this one ties the mod to an ImGui version.

### `imgui_context`

```c
void*(MIRAGE_CALL* imgui_context)(const char* version, uint32_t io_size, uint32_t style_size, uint32_t vertex_size, void** alloc_fn, void** free_fn, void** user);
```

### `setting_draw`

```c
void(MIRAGE_CALL* setting_draw)(MirageSetting* setting, float width);
```

A setting's own control, drawn where the panel is (on_panel; a setting set_visible 0 is only drawn this way)

### `setting_choice`

```c
MirageSetting*(MIRAGE_CALL* setting_choice)(MirageModule* module, const char* name, const char* items, int32_t index, const char* tooltip);
```

A choice (a combo box): `items` like MirageUi::combo's ("A\0B\0"), `index` the default

### `reserved_keys`

```c
void(MIRAGE_CALL* reserved_keys)(MirageMod* mod, const int32_t* vks, int32_t count);
```

Keys the mod is using right now (a TAS session's controls): the menu's own hotkeys don't fire on them. Replaces the mod's previous set; count 0 clears it. Any thread.

`signature` is "float(float, int)": argument types int, float, bool, byte, object, name (arrives as text); return int, float, bool, byte, object or void. Returns the native index to put in a script patch's NativeFunction token (> 0), 0 when it can't be registered (the log says why). The same mod and name again (a hot reload) gets the same index. After the mod's unload its natives return zero. Game thread for the calls.

## Classes from UnrealScript

It is compiled into a script package and the engine loads it: the class (a UClass) spawns and reflects like a cooked one. NULL when it doesn't compile or load: `error` gets why (up to `capacity` bytes; may be NULL). The same source again gives the same class; an edited one (a hot reload) gives a new class of the same name. Game thread.

### `class_load`

```c

```

### `class_define`

```c
MirageObject*(MIRAGE_CALL* class_define)(MirageMod* mod, const char* spec_json, char* error, uint32_t capacity);
```

A class described instead of written, as JSON: {"name": "MyPad", "extends": "Trigger", "placeable": true, "vars": ["float Strength", "var() int Count"], "functions": ["Touch", "function int Count()"], "defaults": ["Strength=1500.0"], "extra": "<more UnrealScript>"}. A function given by name overrides the parent's (its declaration, an empty body); one given as a declaration is new (an empty body too). Their code is the mod's: inject_function(<the class's path>.<function>, "head", ...) reads the parameters and self, sets ReturnValue and returns early. The runtime writes the .uc to mirage\classes\generated\<mod>\ and loads it as class_load does. Game thread.


"Package.Outer.Name" ("MirageBouncePad_1a2b3c4d.MirageBouncePad"): copies up to capacity, returns the full length


Keeps an object from the garbage collector (keep 1) or lets it go (0); the mod's unload lets go of all it kept. A mod's classes go with it: unloading destroys their actors and they can't be spawned until loaded again. Game thread.

## Reversible changes

Game thread. Writes with object_set between change_begin and change_end are a transaction: the value each property had before its first write is kept, and put back by change_revert, and by the runtime when the mod unloads, reloads or crashes (newest transaction first; an object gone since is skipped). Writes outside a transaction aren't recorded (gameplay writes, such as moving the player, stay as they are).

### `change_begin`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* change_begin)(MirageMod* mod, const char* name);
```

Opens one, named for the mod manager's list: its id (> 0), or 0 (one is open already)

### `change_end`

```c
void(MIRAGE_CALL* change_end)(MirageMod* mod);
```

### `change_revert`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* change_revert)(MirageMod* mod, int32_t id);
```

Puts back transaction `id` (-1: every one of the mod's not reverted yet): how many values were put back

### `change_list`

```c
uint32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* change_list)(MirageMod* mod, char* buffer, uint32_t capacity);
```

The mod's transactions as JSON: [{"id", "name", "values": ["Object.Path", ...], "reverted"}]; its full length

## Engine symbols and hooks

The game's functions and globals by name, the runtime's table of them (its symbols.toml, found by pattern at start, and what its own code works out): "ProcessEvent", "Tick", "StaticLoadObject", "GMalloc", ... Any thread.

### `symbol_find`

```c
void*(MIRAGE_CALL* symbol_find)(const char* name);
```

The address (a function, or a global's variable); NULL if the name isn't known or wasn't found on this game

### `detour_symbol`

```c
MirageDetour*(MIRAGE_CALL* detour_symbol)(MirageMod* mod, const char* symbol, void* detour, int32_t priority, void** original);
```

detour_create on a symbol: NULL (and the reason in the log) if it isn't known. Every detour (detour_create's too) runs behind a guard: when it faults in the mod's own code, the call goes on in its *original as if it weren't there, and the mod is stopped and named like a crash in any of its callbacks (its hooks and detours removed).

### `mid_hook_create`

```c
MirageMidHook*(MIRAGE_CALL* mid_hook_create)(MirageMod* mod, void* at, MirageMidHookFn callback, void* user);
```

A hook at an instruction (not only a function's start): `callback` runs there on the thread that runs that code, with the registers. A fault in it skips it from then on and stops the mod. NULL if the place can't be hooked (the reason in the log). Removed with mid_hook_remove, or the mod's unload.


## Kismet

Objects by path (object_find with the class in front: "Sequence Edge_p.TheWorld:PersistentLevel.Main_Sequence"). `level`: only that level's package ("Edge_p"); NULL or "": every loaded level. Copies up to capacity, returns the full length. Game thread.

### `kismet_read`

```c
uint32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* kismet_read)(const char* level, char* buffer, uint32_t capacity);
```

### `kismet_link`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* kismet_link)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* from, const char* output, MirageObject* to, const char* input);
```

Kismet edits. Each is recorded in the mod's open transaction (change_begin; one is opened for the edit when none is), so change_revert and the mod's unload put the graph back. `output` / `input`: a link's description ("Touched", "In") or its index ("0"); NULL or "": the first. The two ops must be in the same sequence. 1: done (kismet_link: or linked already), 0: not (the log says why). Game thread.

### `kismet_unlink`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* kismet_unlink)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* from, const char* output, MirageObject* to, const char* input);
```

### `kismet_create`

```c
MirageObject*(MIRAGE_CALL* kismet_create)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* sequence, const char* class_name);
```

A new op in `sequence`: `class_name` a SequenceOp class ("SeqAct_Log", "Engine.SeqAct_Toggle", a mod's class from class_define extending SequenceAction, its Activated injected). Its links are the class defaults'. Taken out of the sequence again on revert. NULL when it can't (the log says why).

### `kismet_fire`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* kismet_fire)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* event, const char* output, MirageObject* instigator);
```

Fires `event` (a SequenceEvent op) as the engine does when it happens (SequenceEvent.CheckActivate): `output` the output to activate (a description, "Touched", or an index; NULL or "": the first), `instigator` NULL the player's pawn. The event's general conditions apply (enabled, MaxTriggerCount, ReTriggerDelay), not its class's own (a touch event's overlap with its trigger): firing it is the mod saying it happened. 1 when it activated, 0 when the event refused (disabled, fired its MaxTriggerCount, inside its ReTriggerDelay). Not recorded: firing is gameplay, not an edit. Game thread.

### `kismet_trace`

```c
void(MIRAGE_CALL* kismet_trace)(MirageMod* mod, int32_t on);
```

The execution trace: which ops activate, on which tick, how many times (each op's ActivateCount compared tick to tick while any mod has it on; nothing runs while off). kismet_trace_read gives the mod's entries since it last read them as JSON [{"tick", "op", "class", "times"}] (up to 4096 kept), copies up to capacity and returns the full length; the entries are taken only when it all fit. Game thread.

### `kismet_trace_read`

```c
uint32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* kismet_trace_read)(MirageMod* mod, char* buffer, uint32_t capacity);
```

### `movement_transitions`

```c
uint32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* movement_transitions)(char* buffer, uint32_t capacity);
```

The player's last 256 move transitions, oldest first, as JSON [{"tick", "time", "from", "to", "from_name", "to_name", "skipped"}]: EMovement values and their names ("MOVE_Walking"), the engine tick and the level's time (WorldInfo.TimeSeconds); skipped: a mod's PLAYER_STATE callback kept the game from handling it (event_skip). Recorded whether or not a mod listens. Copies up to capacity, returns the full length. Any thread.

## Physics and world queries

Vectors are 3 floats (x, y, z), Unreal units. Bodies through the engine's own functions (SetRBLinearVelocity, AddImpulse, ...). Velocity, impulses, forces, mass and gravity are gameplay: not recorded. A spawned prop and a collision change are recorded in the open transaction (or one of their own): put back on revert and unload. Game thread.

### `physics_body_get`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_body_get)(MirageObject* actor, MirageBody* out);
```

1, or 0 (no such actor). Set out->size first. Actors without a body report location, rotation, velocity.

### `physics_body_set`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_body_set)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* actor, const MirageBody* in, uint32_t fields);
```

`fields`: MIRAGE_BODY_* bits of `in` to apply. 0: the actor has no rigid body (the log says why).

### `physics_impulse`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_impulse)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* actor, const float* impulse, const float* at, int32_t velocity_change);
```

An impulse (mass x velocity; `velocity_change` 1: a velocity change, the mass ignored) or a force (applied over the next physics step) at `at` (NULL: the centre of mass). Wakes the body. 0: no rigid body.

### `physics_force`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_force)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* actor, const float* force, const float* at);
```

### `physics_spawn`

```c
MirageObject*(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_spawn)(MirageMod* mod, const char* mesh, const float* location, const int32_t* rotation, float mass_scale);
```

A physics prop: a KActorSpawnable with the static mesh at `mesh` (any loaded StaticMesh with collision: "PX_LevelEffects2.CardboardBox_01.S_CardboardBox_01"), at `location`, `rotation` 3 ints (NULL: none), simulated and awake, its mass the mesh's times `mass_scale` (0 or 1: the mesh's own). Mass is given here only: the engine reads it from the mesh when it makes the body and never makes it again. The engine caps the mesh's MassScale times this at 100 (a mesh of 50: 2x at most); the scale is capped to match (a warning, and physics_body_get reads what the body got). Destroyed on revert and unload. NULL when it can't (the log says why).

### `physics_collision_get`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_collision_get)(MirageObject* actor);
```

MIRAGE_COLLIDE_ACTORS | MIRAGE_BLOCK_ACTORS | MIRAGE_BLOCK_RIGID_BODY as the actor has them; -1: no such actor

### `physics_collision_set`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_collision_set)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* actor, uint32_t flags);
```

### `world_trace`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* world_trace)(MirageMod* mod, const float* start, const float* end, const float* extent, uint32_t flags, MirageObject* ignore, MirageHit* out);
```

A line trace from `start` to `end`, or a box swept along it (`extent`: half sizes; NULL: a line), through the engine's own line check (UWorld::SingleLineCheck). `flags`: MIRAGE_TRACE_ACTORS. `ignore`: an actor it passes through (NULL: none). 1: hit, 0: nothing, -1: not done (the engine's line check wasn't found, or the mod went over its 4,000 traces this tick: the log says which). Set out->size first.

### `world_overlap`

```c
int32_t(MIRAGE_CALL* world_overlap)(const float* center, float radius, const char* class_name, MirageObject** out, int32_t capacity);
```

Actors in play whose collision bounds touch the sphere (bounds, not shapes), of `class_name` or a subclass (NULL or "": any), as of this tick (an actor spawned now is found from the next). Fills up to capacity, returns how many there are.

### `physics_joint`

```c
MirageObject*(MIRAGE_CALL* physics_joint)(MirageMod* mod, MirageObject* a, MirageObject* b, const float* location, const int32_t* rotation, int32_t kind, float break_threshold);
```

A joint between two bodies (`b` NULL: `a` held to the world) at `location`, `rotation` 3 ints (NULL: none; a hinge turns about its X axis), MIRAGE_JOINT_BALL or _HINGE, breaking under `break_threshold` (0: never): the engine's RB_ConstraintActorSpawnable and InitConstraint. Removed on revert and unload. NULL when it can't (the log says why).

## Types

### `MirageLogLevel`

A control in a module's settings panel */

```c
typedef enum MirageLogLevel {
    MIRAGE_LOG_DEBUG = 0,
    MIRAGE_LOG_INFO = 1,
    MIRAGE_LOG_WARN = 2,
    MIRAGE_LOG_ERROR = 3
} MirageLogLevel;
```

### `MirageSettingType`

setting_type: what a setting holds *

```c
typedef enum MirageSettingType {
    MIRAGE_SETTING_BOOL = 0,
    MIRAGE_SETTING_INT = 1,
    MIRAGE_SETTING_FLOAT = 2,
    MIRAGE_SETTING_STRING = 3,
    MIRAGE_SETTING_CHOICE = 4,
    MIRAGE_SETTING_KEY = 5,
    MIRAGE_SETTING_COLOR = 6,   /* setting_get_int: the color packed as the draw functions take it (0xAABBGGRR) */
    MIRAGE_SETTING_UNKNOWN = -1
} MirageSettingType;
```

### `MirageModuleDesc`

What a module is: filled by the mod, copied by module_register *

```c
typedef struct MirageModuleDesc {
    uint32_t size;                  /* sizeof(MirageModuleDesc) */
    const char* name;               /* Unique in the menu ("Hello"); the config saves it under this name */
    const char* tab;                /* Menu column ("Mods" if NULL); created when no module had it yet */
    const char* description;        /* One line, shown on hover (may be NULL) */
    int32_t order;                  /* Position in the column, lower first (100 if 0) */
    int32_t key;                    /* Default toggle key (virtual-key code), 0 = none */
    uint32_t flags;                 /* MIRAGE_MODULE_* */
    void* user;                     /* Passed back to every callback */
    MirageCallback on_enable;       /* Each may be NULL */
    MirageCallback on_disable;      /* Also on unload: undo what the module changed */
    MirageCallback on_tick;         /* Game thread, every tick while on */
    MirageCallback on_render;       /* Render thread, every frame while on */
    MirageCallback on_trigger;      /* Action modules: clicked or key pressed */
    /* Appended in step 9 (a mod built before has a smaller `size`: the runtime doesn't read these) */
    MirageCallback on_panel;        /* Render thread: draws (with api->ui()) in the module's settings panel, below its
                                       settings, while the panel is open. The panel's width: ui->content_width() */
} MirageModuleDesc;
```

### `MirageValueType`

A value read from or written to a game object or a call, by dotted path ("Location.Z", "NewLocation", "ReturnValue") *

```c
typedef enum MirageValueType {
    MIRAGE_VALUE_NONE = 0,      /* Nothing there (the path didn't resolve) */
    MIRAGE_VALUE_BOOL = 1,      /* i: 0/1 */
    MIRAGE_VALUE_INT = 2,       /* i (bytes and enums too) */
    MIRAGE_VALUE_FLOAT = 3,     /* f */
    MIRAGE_VALUE_OBJECT = 4,    /* o (NULL: none) */
    MIRAGE_VALUE_TEXT = 5,      /* text: a name or a string (written: names; strings only as a call's parameters,
                                   in a call the mod makes with call_begin) */
    MIRAGE_VALUE_STRUCT = 6,    /* A struct: reach its members with a longer path ("Location" -> "Location.X") */
    MIRAGE_VALUE_ARRAY = 7      /* An array: i = how many elements; reach one with "[n]" ("StreamingLevels[0]",
                                   0-based). Elements are read and written, the array isn't resized */
} MirageValueType;
```

### `MirageValue`

```c
typedef struct MirageValue {
    int32_t type;               /* MIRAGE_VALUE_* */
    int32_t i;
    float f;
    MirageObject* o;
    char text[256];             /* UTF-8, cut at 255 bytes */
} MirageValue;
```

### `MirageEvent`

A checkpoint restart: the player is a new pawn in the same level. Objects of the old player are gone *

```c
typedef struct MirageEvent {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageEvent) */
    int32_t type;               /* MIRAGE_EVENT_* */
    int32_t value, value2;
    float number;
    const char* text;           /* Valid during the callback; "" if none */
    MirageObject* object;       /* The event's object (MIRAGE_EVENT_ACTOR_*), else NULL. Appended (step 14): check
                                   size >= offsetof(MirageEvent, object) + sizeof(void*) before reading it */
} MirageEvent;
```

### `MirageHandle`

---- World access (step 14) ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- A MirageObject is the object's address: once the object is gone, another object can come at the same address and in the same slot of the engine's object list, and the old pointer would quietly mean the new object. A MirageHandle also keeps what identifies the object (its slot, its name, its class): handle_object gives the object back only while all of it still matches, else NULL. Plain data: keep it as long as you like, across ticks and level loads. *

```c
typedef struct MirageHandle {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageHandle) */
    MirageObject* object;
    uint32_t slot;              /* Its index in the engine's object list */
    int32_t name_index, name_number;    /* Its name (an FName) */
    MirageObject* object_class;
} MirageHandle;
```

### `MirageRegisters`

mid_hook_create: the registers at the hooked instruction, given to the callback, which may change them (esp is read-only). continue_at: 0 runs the instructions the hook replaced and goes on after them; an address skips them and goes on there with the registers as left. *

```c
typedef struct MirageRegisters {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageRegisters), set by the runtime */
    uint32_t eax, ecx, edx, ebx, esp, ebp, esi, edi;
    uint32_t eflags;
    uint32_t continue_at;
} MirageRegisters;
```

### `MirageMovement`

movement_get: what the player is doing (step 4 of the next ten steps). The moves are TdGame's EMovement values (MOVE_Walking 1, MOVE_Falling 2, MOVE_Jump 11, ...: the generated SDK lists them); move_object is the current move's object (TdPawn.Moves[move]: a TdMove_*, its tuning properties readable by path). *

```c
typedef struct MirageMovement {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageMovement) */
    int32_t move;               /* TdPawn.MovementState */
    int32_t previous_move;      /* TdPawn.OldMovementState */
    int32_t physics;            /* Actor.Physics (EPhysics: PHYS_Walking 1, PHYS_Falling 2, ...) */
    float velocity[3];
    float speed;                /* Horizontal speed (units a second) */
    MirageObject* move_object;
} MirageMovement;
```

### `MirageBody`

physics_body_get / physics_body_set (step 6 of the next ten steps): a rigid body (a KActor, a prop) *

```c
typedef struct MirageBody {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageBody) */
    float location[3];
    int32_t rotation[3];        /* Pitch, yaw, roll (65536 = a full turn) */
    float linear_velocity[3];   /* Unreal units a second */
    float angular_velocity[3];  /* Radians a second */
    float mass_scale;           /* Get only: the mass scale a prop was spawned with (1: the mesh's own mass) */
    float gravity_scale;        /* RB_BodyInstance.CustomGravityFactor */
    int32_t awake;              /* Simulating now (not asleep) */
    int32_t simulated;          /* Get only: Physics is PHYS_RigidBody and there is a body */
} MirageBody;
```

### `MirageHit`

world_trace: what the trace hit *

```c
typedef struct MirageHit {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageHit) */
    int32_t hit;                /* 1: something was hit (else the rest is zero) */
    MirageObject* actor;        /* The actor hit; the world's own geometry (BSP, static meshes): the level's WorldInfo */
    MirageObject* component;    /* The primitive component hit */
    float location[3];
    float normal[3];
    float time;                 /* Where along the trace, 0..1 */
    char bone[64];              /* A skeletal mesh's bone, else "" */
    MirageObject* material;     /* With MIRAGE_TRACE_MATERIAL: the material hit (a MaterialInterface) when the engine
                                   reports one (BSP; static meshes often don't), else NULL */
    MirageObject* phys_material; /* ... and the PhysicalMaterial hit (the hit's, else the material's), else NULL */
} MirageHit;
```

### `MirageActorQuery`

actors_query: which actors (every field optional; zero = any). Actors of the levels in play (the persistent level and the visible streaming levels), from the runtime's per-tick actor lists: no walk of the whole object list. *

```c
typedef struct MirageActorQuery {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageActorQuery) */
    const char* class_name;     /* "TdBotPawn", or by path "TdGame.TdBotPawn": that class and its subclasses */
    const char* tag;            /* Actor.Tag */
    const char* name;           /* The object's name ("TdBotPawn_3") */
    MirageObject* near_object;  /* With radius > 0: around this actor's Location ... */
    float x, y, z;              /* ... or around this point (when near_object is NULL) */
    float radius;               /* > 0: only within this distance; the results then come nearest first */
} MirageActorQuery;
```

### `MirageToken`

A function's bytecode, open for editing (owned by the mod) *

```c
typedef struct MirageToken {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageToken): set it before script_get / script_set / script_add */
    int32_t kind;               /* The token's kind: script_kind("FloatConst"), script_kind_name(kind) */
    int32_t native_index;       /* NativeFunction: the native's index (171: float * float, 174: float + float) */
    int32_t int_value;          /* IntConst */
    float floats[3];            /* FloatConst: floats[0]; VectorConst */
    int32_t ints[3];            /* RotationConst */
    MirageObject* object;       /* The object operand: a variable's property, a function, a class (NULL: none) */
    MirageObject* object2;      /* A second one (StructMember's struct, Context's property) */
    char name[64];              /* The name operand (VirtualFunction's function, NameConst); written: an existing name */
    uint16_t word, word2;       /* Skips and jump targets as decoded (script_apply recomputes them) */
    uint8_t byte_value, byte_value2, reserved[2];   /* ByteConst / IntConstByte, cast type, flags */
    int32_t target;             /* A jump added by the mod: the token it goes to (-1: as decoded, -2: the script's end) */
    uint32_t memory_offset;     /* Where it was in the code when opened (read only; 0 for an added token) */
    char text[256];             /* StringConst / UnicodeStringConst, UTF-8 */
} MirageToken;
```

### `MirageWorldVertex`

---- 3D drawing in the world (step 9) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Flat-colored triangles and lines in world units, drawn by the runtime's Direct3D renderer inside the game's frame (hidden behind the world where its depth buffer is there, else an overlay), with the engine's own view. One scene at a time (the last mod to set it): the collision view's. Layers are replaced whole; set them from the game thread. *

```c
typedef struct MirageWorldVertex {
    float x, y, z;
    uint32_t color;             /* 0xAARRGGBB (Direct3D's order, not the draw functions') */
} MirageWorldVertex;
```

### `MirageWorldLabel`

```c
typedef struct MirageWorldLabel {
    float x, y, z;
    uint32_t color;             /* 0xAARRGGBB */
    const char* text;           /* Copied */
} MirageWorldLabel;
```

### `MirageWorldMesh`

```c
typedef struct MirageWorldMesh {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageWorldMesh) */
    const MirageWorldVertex* triangles;     /* A triangle list: 3 vertices each */
    uint32_t triangle_vertices;
    const MirageWorldVertex* lines;         /* A line list: 2 vertices each */
    uint32_t line_vertices;
    const MirageWorldLabel* labels;         /* Text at a world position (MIRAGE_WORLD_SCENE only) */
    uint32_t label_count;
    uint32_t shapes;            /* For the stats: how many shapes it is */
    float build_ms;             /* For the stats: how long building it took */
} MirageWorldMesh;
```

### `MirageWorldStyle`

Large world geometry; its faces at static_opacity *

```c
typedef struct MirageWorldStyle {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageWorldStyle) */
    float opacity;              /* Faces (outlines are opaque) */
    int32_t overlay;            /* 1: always on top (no depth test) */
    float fov_offset;           /* Degrees added to the camera's */
    float aspect;               /* 0: from the viewport */
    float near_plane;           /* Used when the engine's is unknown */
    float static_opacity;       /* Faces of MIRAGE_WORLD_STATIC */
} MirageWorldStyle;
```

### `MirageWorldStats`

```c
typedef struct MirageWorldStats {
    uint32_t size;              /* sizeof(MirageWorldStats): set it before world_draw_stats */
    int32_t drawn;              /* The last frame drew something */
    int32_t in_scene;           /* ... inside the game's frame (depth tested); 0: as an overlay */
    int32_t overlay_fallback;   /* The game's scene pass wasn't found: overlay only */
    uint32_t triangles, lines, shapes, labels, static_triangles, static_lines;
    float build_ms;
} MirageWorldStats;
```

### `MirageMemoryStats`

```c
typedef struct MirageMemoryStats {
    uint32_t size;                  /* sizeof(MirageMemoryStats): set it before the call */
    int32_t pressure;               /* MIRAGE_MEMORY_* */
    uint64_t process_private;       /* The process's commit charge (bytes) */
    uint64_t process_working_set;
    uint64_t address_free;          /* Free address space (a 32-bit game: what runs out first) */
    uint64_t address_largest_free;  /* Its largest block; 0 = not measured yet */
    uint64_t menu_heap;             /* The menu's own heap, live */
    uint64_t mod_lua;               /* This mod's Lua state(s), 0 for a native mod (its own CRT is its own) */
} MirageMemoryStats;
```
